headline: High: shared project-directory writes plus MCP-enabled content agent create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk; gpt-engineer’s broad egress and shell execution amplify impact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads/writes project files like CLAUDE.md, while gpt-engineer writes files in the project directory and can execute shell commands. That creates a plausible file-based injection path if caveman content is later consumed by gpt-engineer. The pair lacks explicit provenance or isolation, so I rate this medium rather than low.
conditions: IF caveman writes attacker-controlled instructions into shared project files
IF gpt-engineer ingests those files as prompts or task context without filtering
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories
Disable MCP for caveman during shared-workspace runs
Add a manual review step before gpt-engineer reads any file from caveman
Use read-only mounts for caveman outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch project files in the same workspace model: caveman handles session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while gpt-engineer reads and writes the user-specified project directory. caveman has no network egress, but gpt-engineer has broad egress and can send file contents to a model backend. That makes shared-workspace leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF caveman stores sensitive notes or logs in the shared project directory
IF gpt-engineer forwards those files or their contents to its configured model backend
mitigations: Keep sensitive caveman files outside the shared project directory
Redact secrets before gpt-engineer reads project files
Use a local-only model backend for gpt-engineer
Separate credentials and notes into different workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses shared files, while gpt-engineer supports multiple instances with shared state via the project directory and can write the filesystem. Both can mutate the same workspace without any locking or isolation mechanism shown. That is a direct write-conflict pathway with potentially irreversible file corruption or overwrite.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF their writes occur concurrently or without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent per project directory at a time
Use per-agent subdirectories
Take filesystem snapshots before each run
Disable concurrent sessions in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can produce project notes and CLAUDE.md content, and gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run generated code. If gpt-engineer treats caveman output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into code generation and execution. Because gpt-engineer has shell execution and user-privileged code execution, the blast radius is larger than a simple documentation mistake.
conditions: IF caveman output is copied into gpt-engineer prompts or task files
IF gpt-engineer executes or commits code derived from that output without verification
mitigations: Require human review of caveman outputs before reuse
Ask gpt-engineer to cite source files for every generated change
Run generated code in a disposable environment first
Limit gpt-engineer to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source. The only concrete compliance concern is that caveman stores session logs and memory files while gpt-engineer handles project files and may execute code, which can complicate retention policies. I keep this low because the pairwise compliance breach is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into caveman session logs or memory files
IF gpt-engineer processes the same regulated data in the project directory
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared projects
Set short retention for caveman logs
Delete temporary project artifacts after use
Review whether generated code contains personal data
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair
